entities.summary: Glycon of Athens (b. 100 BCE, Athens) was a musician or composer of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Athens. Known for his work in the fields of painters and sculptors, Glycon's compositions were performed at the Theater of Dionysus. The city of Athens, under the patronage of the Roman Empire, was a hub of artistic innovation during this period. Glycon's music was likely performed in the context of religious and cultural events, further emphasizing the significance of his work in the cultural landscape of ancient Athens. The legacy of Glycon of Athens can be seen in the development of Western classical music, with his compositions influencing later generations of musicians. The 60 BCE date of his death marked the end of an era, but his contributions to the arts continue to be celebrated and studied today.
